candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
The files and brief are attached. After reviewing them, please let us know what you think.

For the newest Microsoft Word versions on Windows PC, we need an experienced template specialist to assess, repair, and enhance a set of Word templates. These are intended for real users, so visual quality alone is insufficient: they must also remain technically reliable, particularly when users copy and paste material from legacy templates into the new templates.

**The help we would appreciate**

Please complete the following before proposing the work:

1\. Read the entire brief carefully
2\. Examine the latest template documents and their support files
3\. Respond with:
• a fixed project price
• a proposed timeline
• any early observations or risks

⸻

Scope of Work

1\. Test the existing templates

Confirm through user and functional testing that the templates are correctly constructed and dependable during ordinary daily use.

Testing must cover:
• styles
• list behavior
• indentation logic
• tab behavior
• line breaks
• tables
• columns
• copy-paste behavior
• overall formatting stability

⸻

2\. Apply the new styles to every template

Across the complete template set, consistently implement the style system specified in:

new\_styles\_for\_implementation\_nxq

⸻

3\. Recommend improvements

After examining the templates, identify both:
• need-to-have improvements
• nice-to-have improvements

Recommendations may address missing functionality, structural changes, usability enhancements, stability improvements, or technical corrections that would make the templates easier and more reliable to use.

⸻

Environment

Current Microsoft Word versions on PC will be the operating environment for every template.

Optimize the files for:
• modern Word for Windows
• real user editing behavior
• stable use by multiple users

⸻

Customer Design Feedback to Implement

A. Tab functionality and indentation logic

In every relevant list style, users must be able to create sub-levels naturally with the Tab key.

Ensure that:
• every list style supports intuitive sub-level indentation
• the hierarchy stays clean and structured
• list levels follow the vertical-alignment logic in the brief
• nested levels remain consistently aligned throughout each document

(Use New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_nxq for the design guidance.)

B. Graphic bullet design

Revise the bullets so that:
• their size is proportionate to the text size
• their appearance is visually balanced
• they are vertically middle-aligned with the text
• they scale naturally when the font size changes

C. Rename every style

If doing so helps resolve copy-paste issues, rename all relevant template styles with this prefix:

NXQ -

Examples:
• NXQ - Heading 1
• NXQ - Body Text
• NXQ - Bullet List

Use the prefix for all relevant active styles, including:
• headings
• body text
• quotes
• list styles
• table-related styles
• other active styles used in the templates

⸻

Customer Error Feedback to Resolve

1\. Compatibility and copy-paste stability

Moving content from legacy templates into the new ones currently creates major formatting problems. Use these supplied legacy files for testing:
• Archive\_r7.docx
• Archive\_r12.docx

Test this workflow and make it as stable as technically possible.

2\. Line break issues

Users are unable to create manual line breaks reliably after pasted material. Correct that behavior.

3\. Table and column integrity

Pasting currently causes both of these problems:
• the right-hand column can move beyond the page margins
• table layouts can break

Keep the table structure locked and stable inside the page layout.

4\. Style break prevention

Determine whether template styles can be prevented from breaking, or at least made less likely to break, when users paste text from legacy documents. Word does have limitations, but the setup should be as robust as possible within those constraints.

⸻

Testing Requirements

Thoroughly test:
• all list levels
• bullet lists
• numbered lists
• multilevel list behavior
• tab and indent behavior
• table behavior
• column behavior
• copy-paste from legacy templates
• manual line breaks after pasting
• overall layout stability

Specific test requirement

In particular, test copying and pasting from old NXQ templates into V27. Verify that:
• the layout remains stable
• styles behave predictably
• Tab functionality is intuitive for end users
• list hierarchy remains aligned and usable

⸻

Deliverables

Your proposal should provide:
1\. A fixed project price
2\. An estimated timeline
3\. Notes covering recommended need-to-have and nice-to-have improvements

At delivery, we expect:
• updated template files
• consistent NXQ style naming (maybe)
• the new styles implemented according to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_nxq
• improved list behavior
• better paste stability wherever technically possible

candidates.text:
Salam Jonas,

Please let me know what you think about this first round of customer feedback, which I have grouped by issue below.

Field behavior and text entry:
• Proposal (Indstilling) placeholder fields: Unlike in the Executive Summary, clicking the "insert" fields—Advantages, settings, attachments, headline, and date—does not automatically clear the existing text.
• Guidance (Vejledning) reflections: Under "(write own reflections, if any)," the placeholder text has the same failure to clear automatically as in the Proposal fields.
• Board Seminar (Bestyrelsesseminar) agenda: The "(insert agenda)" field has the same automatic-clearing issue as the Proposal fields.
• Proposal text boxes: When the boxes on the left, including the headline, run out of room, words do not wrap automatically. The right-hand column is pushed farther to the right instead.
• Proposal line breaks: Because automatic wrapping is missing, users are forced to insert line breaks manually. A normal line break (hard return) creates excessive spacing for continuous text, even though that spacing works well between bullet points. A soft return (Shift\+Enter) gives the correct result, but I doubt our colleagues know how to use it.
• Board Seminar multi-line support: Under "Item and Title," users must be able to enter multiple lines, including through manual line breaks.

Layout and formatting:
• Guidance margins: The margins beneath the "(short description)" section are not fixed. Without manual line breaks, the "pencil" icon is gradually cut off. Can fixed margins be set there?
• Guidance theme description: This has the same hard-return spacing problem as the Proposal.
• Board Meeting (Bestyrelsesmøde) alignment: Compared with "Topic," "Proposal," and "Start time," "Item and Title" is not aligned correctly.
• Board Meeting formatting: An extra horizontal line or border appears whenever I add a line immediately after a "Topic." Adding a line anywhere else works as intended.

Date functionality:
• Proposal: Could the date functionality used in the "Board Seminar" document also be implemented here?
• Board Meeting: Is it possible to use the date functionality from the "Board Seminar" document here as well?

Master:
• Review: Because the bullet sizes and spacing still look incorrect on my screen, we need to review them with Tariq.
• Tables: Please provide an explanation or walkthrough showing how the tables work.
• Color palette: The full set of currently available colors should not all be offered as options.

candidates.text:
Before estimating the work required to create the Power Point template, please review the attached customer design and send your thoughts.

These are my initial questions and feedback:

Tariq:

At first glance, the design is well-structured, and the font sizes are exactly right.

I'll examine it more closely later from a technical perspective and, of course, provide an estimate as well.

Questions
Does the value after the slash in the specified font sizes (72/88) represent line height?

For the front page, section dividers, or paragraph slides, shouldn't there be a 16:9 background image with text placed over it?

A logo typically does not appear on every single slide. Is having it everywhere the preferred approach here?

Are the splash placeholder images intended to work as masks?

The spacing from the heading to the body text differs between slides 28 and 31. Was that deliberate?

To Be Investigated
Slides 7 and 19 need more thought. If users must be able to add multiple bullets themselves, a bullet containing highlighted text with body text underneath might not be feasible. Restricting the layout to just two could make it work, but I assume that limitation is not wanted.

Design Questions
In many places, the text has been designed perfectly against the grid. That relationship will naturally change if a user adds one bullet point rather than two.

When the count rises to more than two, the text will automatically shrink to create enough room.

This is the point where real-world usage comes into play, so let's monitor it and see how the layout behaves.

Please Send
Could you provide these graphic elements in vector format?

The bullet point

The shapes used for the selected splashes
